newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada board approves Federated pipeline project.
newsitem.headline: Canada board approves Federated pipeline project.

text.p: Canada's National Energy Board said on Thursday it approved Federated Pipe Lines (Northern) Ltd's application to build a crude oil and natural gas liquids line to Belloy, Alberta from Taylor, British Columbia.

The pipeline, one of several proposed in the region, would consist of about 173 km of 10-inch pipe to move oil, segregated condensate, ethane plus and propane plus to a proposed Alberta pipeline at Belloy from facilities at Taylor in northeastern B.C.
Construction of the pipeline, which would cost an estimated C$40.8 million, was slated to start this summer and completion was scheduled for the winter of 1997-98, the NEB said.
Its initial delivery capacity was set at 52,000 barrels per day.
Federated is co-owned by Anderson Exploration Ltd and Imperial Oil Ltd.
